previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, hepatitis C, and alcohol dependence was admitted for acute shortness of breath and volume overload after missing his medications for a week. He reported ongoing alcohol use and recent psychosocial stress. Elevated BNP and chest imaging confirmed acute on chronic heart failure, and he was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned back to oral torsemide. Alcohol withdrawal was monitored with CIWA scoring, peaking at 10; he declined an additional hospital stay despite risks. Mild epigastric pain was managed as suspected alcoholic gastritis. He improved clinically, with reduced edema and stable vitals, and was discharged home with continued heart failure medications and strong recommendations to avoid alcohol and engage in detox and counseling services.
